tagline.text: El Nido's best sunset beach, where the sun sets between limestone islands

location.label: Location
location.text: Bulbulungan coast near El Nido town, Palawan

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,200 (transport, drinks and a meal, per person)

children.text: Las Cabanas Beach is a golden-sand beach about 10–15 minutes by tricycle from El Nido town. It is famous for the sun setting behind the silhouettes of limestone islands, and you can wait for the sunset at your leisure at the beachfront bars and restaurants.

Las Cabañas Beach lies a short way from El Nido town along the coastal road in Palawan. Local maps place it on the coast of Bulbulungan village in El Nido. The name comes from a small resort of the same name, and it runs a few hundred meters from neighboring Marimegmeg Beach, so it is easy to see both at once.

What made this beach famous is the evening rather than the daytime scenery. The sun sinks between the silhouettes of limestone islands across the water and steep cliffs, and the sky turns orange, pink and purple. Travelers' reviews describe the sunset here as among the best views in the Philippines. The most efficient way to use it is as a place to rest between island-hopping tours during the day and as a sunset spot in the evening.

The sand is not the fine white sand of El Nido's other beaches but closer to golden. During the blue hour (the blue light just before nightfall) and just before sunset, the sand glistens and photos come out well. Small bars, restaurants and bungalows line the beachfront, and some set out sunbeds and tables on the sand. At the beach, many people swim, play volleyball or frisbee, sunbathe, read, or pass the time with a cold beer. You may also see local children swimming alongside tourists in the warm sea.

The beach is known not to charge an entrance fee. However, resorts and private areas may charge for facility use, and how things are run can change, so confirm locally. Even within El Nido, some stretches have weak phone signal, and ATMs are only in town, so bring cash ahead of time.

Looking out to sea from the beach, you see the sun sink between the islands and cliffs. Arrive one to two hours before sunset to claim a spot and wait for the sunset. If you bring a towel and a drink, you can watch comfortably from the sand.

Marimegmeg Beach, also called Vanilla Beach, is a few hundred meters from Las Cabanas. You can walk between the two beaches. Marimegmeg tends to be crowded in the daytime, and a review suggests going before 10 a.m. to see it quietly.

blocks.title: Walking to Depeldet Island at low tide

children.text: One review says you can walk to Depeldet Island at low tide. Depending on the tide, the path may be cut off or get deeper, so check the timing and safety with local staff or a boatman before you go.
Bars and restaurants line the beach, so you can have a drink or a light meal while waiting for the sunset. Many reviews say prices are quite high, so bring snacks if your budget is tight.

One guide says that if you walk a few hundred meters from Las Cabanas toward Dolarog Beach Resort, you reach a quieter beach with a view of Pinagbuyutan Island. Check locally whether the path is passable and accessible.
There is reportedly a zipline in this area for adventurous visitors. Whether it is operating, and its prices and safety rules, can change, so check for yourself.

blocks.title: A night at a beach resort

children.text: At the point at the end of the beach there is a simple cottage resort, and reviews say you can see both sunset and sunrise right in front of it. The facilities are basic, and air-conditioning, hot water and electricity may be limited, so adjust your expectations.

It gets dark on the way back, so arrange a round-trip tricycle in advance or get the driver's contact number. Before the sunset, stroll slowly between Marimegmeg and Las Cabanas and enjoy the evening mood. At low tide the sand flat widens, making walking easier.

If it is low tide, walk carefully toward Depeldet Island. Check the tide and safety first.
The sun is strong and shade is scarce in the daytime, so bring a hat and sunscreen.
There are direct flights from Manila (MNL) to El Nido Airport (ENI), and airlines and times change by season. Direct flights are known to cost more.
It is also common to fly to Puerto Princesa International Airport (PPS) and continue to El Nido by land. Several airlines fly daily from Manila to Puerto Princesa.

Reviews say the tricycle drops you in front of shops on the main road, and you go down stairs from there to reach the beach. If your accommodation is on the beach, you may have to carry your luggage along a sandy path.

So the driver does not confuse the entrance, name the Marimegmeg entrance or the Las Cabanas resort. Asking your accommodation staff where tricycles stop and where the stairs are is the most accurate way.
The exact location and access can change, so ask the driver or your accommodation first.
You can walk between Marimegmeg and Las Cabanas.
Just before sunset, many tricycles run from town carrying people to see the sunset.

Las Cabanas is best in the dry season, November–May. The sky is clear, the sunset is vivid and the sea is calm for swimming. In the rainy season, June–October, clouds can block the sunset and the waves can get higher.

During the day, it is common to go two to three hours before sunset to enjoy both the daytime sun and the sunset. You can also go in the morning to see quiet Marimegmeg first. The width of the beach changes with the tide, so check before you visit.

To avoid missing the sunset, check the sunset time with your accommodation or an app and leave one to two hours earlier. Even on cloudy days the sky sometimes colors just before sunset, so it is worth going even if the weather looks dull.

The beach itself has simple cottage resorts and bungalows, and the town has places to stay in every price range. Beach accommodation may have limited air-conditioning, hot water and electricity, so check the facilities before booking. If you need a large hotel, the town or the Corong Corong area is more convenient. Reviews describe options in town from small guesthouses near the center to mid-range places with a pool and upscale places with notable design. Names and prices change every year, so choose using the latest reviews on booking sites.

Bars and restaurants line the beach, but many reviews say prices are higher than in town. People order a drink timed to the sunset, and some who want to drink liquor or wine separately buy it at shops in town beforehand. If you order food at a restaurant, you feel less awkward occupying a seat for a long time.

At the Marimegmeg side, sunbeds can reportedly be rented on the beach and local bars line it. Reviews say prices are higher than in town, so it is more economical to buy simple water and snacks at shops in town. Commercial facilities near the beach keep changing, so confirm locally whether places are open when you visit.
To watch the sunset, arrive one to two hours before sunset and claim a spot.
Bring a towel or a thin mat, insect repellent and a power bank.
Prepare plenty of cash. ATMs are only in town and sometimes have long lines or run out.
If you arrange a round-trip tricycle, the ride back is easier.
Pack light. There are stairs and sandy paths.
Marimegmeg is crowded in the daytime, so go early in the morning if you want it quiet.
Keep your belongings in sight, and have someone watch them when you swim.
Phone signal is weak in some stretches, so set a meeting time and place in advance.
If you bring a volleyball or frisbee, you can make good use of your time at the beach.
The beach is busiest around sunset, so once you claim a spot, do not leave your things for long.
Beach width and swimming conditions change with the tide and waves. Always check local information before walking toward Depeldet Island.
After sunset it is dark, and the stairs and sandy path can be dangerous, so prepare a flashlight or phone light.
Waves can get higher in the rainy season, so follow safety signs and local guidance.
Beach facilities and prices can change, and some areas may be private, so check.
Carrying heavy bags down the stairs is hard, so use a porter or pack light.
Do not leave trash behind; take it with you.
Phone signal is weak in some parts of the beach, so agree on a place to meet if you get separated from your group.
Vanilla Beach, a few hundred meters from Las Cabanas. You can walk there, and mornings are quiet.
A long, wide beach you visit on a day trip from El Nido. Rather than combining it with Las Cabanas on the same day, it is better to go separately.
